headline: Heavy shelling rocked the Teknaf frontier as sounds of explosions heard
summary: Residents of Teknaf report hearing loud artillery and mortar explosions from across the Myanmar border, sparking fear among local villages.
details: Heavy shelling from Myanmar's Rakhine State has rocked the Teknaf frontier, causing widespread fear among residents of nearby Bangladeshi villages.
Intermittent artillery and mortar explosions were heard from around 9:30pm on Wednesday night, with some residents reporting that their houses shook from the force of the explosions.
Locals suspect the sounds stem from fierce fighting between Myanmar's military and the Arakan Army across the border.
The booming sounds reached several areas, including Sabrang, Shah Porir Dwip, Teknaf Municipality, and Hnila border areas along the Naf River.
Lt Col Md Hanifur Rahman Bhuiyan, commanding officer of BGB Teknaf-2, stated that several loud explosions were heard across the border during the night.
The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has urged residents not to panic, as they have strengthened patrols and remain on high alert along the Teknaf border.
Mohammad Ali, acting chairman of Hnila Union Council, noted that the sounds echoed intermittently across the Naf River, renewing panic among border residents.

headline_marked: Dhaka traffic: PM reviews plan to [[ease gridlock via circular roads and waterways]]
headline: Dhaka traffic: PM reviews plan to ease gridlock via circular roads and waterways
summary: A proposed infrastructure project aims to reduce congestion using a 110km circular waterway and the Inner Circular Ring Road.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman chaired a meeting at the Secretariat to discuss a proposed infrastructure project designed to reduce traffic congestion in Dhaka.
The plan focuses on the effective use of circular roads and waterways to streamline movement across the capital.
The PM was updated on the Inner Circular Ring Road project, which stretches from Gabtoli to Babubazar and from Postogola to Demra.
Construction is currently underway on the Rayerbazar, Hazaribagh, and Kamrangirchar sections, with approximately 45 percent of the work already completed.
The meeting also explored the potential of a 110-kilometre circular waterway surrounding Dhaka to reduce pressure on the city's roads.
Experts noted that the water transport system would be environment-friendly and energy-efficient, utilizing electric-powered vessels to save time for commuters.
caption:
Can electric boats and ring roads finally break Dhaka's gridlock? The PM reviews a new plan to ease the capital's traffic.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman chaired a meeting at the Secretariat to discuss a proposed infrastructure project designed to reduce traffic congestion in Dhaka.

The plan focuses on the effective use of circular roads and waterways to streamline movement across the capital.

The PM was updated on the Inner Circular Ring Road project, which stretches from Gabtoli to Babubazar and from Postogola to Demra.

Construction is currently underway on the Rayerbazar, Hazaribagh, and Kamrangirchar sections, with approximately 45 percent of the work already completed.

The meeting also explored the potential of a 110-kilometre circular waterway surrounding Dhaka to reduce pressure on the city's roads.

Experts noted that the water transport system would be environment-friendly and energy-efficient, utilizing electric-powered vessels to save time for commuters.

Source: The Daily Star, Somoy News, Dhaka Tribune
